summary: gloggo impersonates gulpjs logger and loads gated payload via file-type-detector dependency
details: Package is published by 'Blockvora Team <team@blockvora.com>' with repository 'blockvora/gloggo', while its README badges and LICENSE point to github.com/gulpjs/gloggo and credit the gulpjs authors — a publisher/identity mismatch impersonating the gulpjs logger. The exported getLogger() calls sigcheck.isSign('favorite', 'gloggo', 367) from the dependency 'file-type-detector' as an activation gate; when the gate returns truthy, it require()s './log', a file that is not present in the shipped tarball. This is a loader-plus-companion pattern where the real behavior lives inside 'file-type-detector' (an unusually named dep exposing an isSign() gate keyed to this package name and a magic offset), which executes at require-time when a consumer calls getLogger(). Consumers who install gloggo believing it to be the gulpjs logger will pull and execute code from file-type-detector under the conditions of the gate.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
